### You poke at the essence and visions overtake your sight.  
  
*Belonging. Hunger. Rejection...*  
  
The seer's home. The tower.  
  
Rest. Breathe. Peace...  
  
He teaches, I learn. Tyria...so vast.  
  
I hunger. Worry. I explain.  
  
Dismissal. Unbalanced, he says.  
  
Speaks of ascension, Waiting Sorrow, equilibrium.  
  
I must feed. I hunger.  
  
Why is he so empty? Alone?  
  
Hunger. Nothing.  
  
HUNGER!  
  
Hunting. Blood. Centaur village, drained. Regret...  
  
He watches. Disdain. Fear.  
  
I plead. He does not hear. Shouting.  
  
Tyria vanishes.  
  
Falling, flying, dirt. Home. Nayos...

Any analysis of the Searing would be incomplete without exploring the history of magical escalation in conflicts throughout Tyria. Attempting to determine which party was justified in using overwhelming force does not help us predict future catastrophes, but a pattern emerges when we examine who had reason to believe that they were cornered.  
  
This belief does not need to be accurate to lead to tragedy, and taking the final step is rarely a sound tactical decision. Once one party has used devastating arcane weapons to claim a decisive victory, the long-term results are more often a chain of reckless last stands and societal collapse.

strings.en:
Astral Ward, friends.  

The news may have reached your fireside, but I am writing to inform you of the loss of our ally. Mabon was a caretaker before he was a leader; he loved this world and all of you.  

Even I...struggle to find the right words to express what he meant to us. Mabon found me after I'd become a husk of a man; a shaman without a spirit to follow. He offered me warmth when my soul was bedrock. He guided me to new purpose. I will mourn.  

Eparch's march against Tyria took him from us, and that fight is long from concluded. Even as we push on—and I promise you that we will fight—take a moment to reflect. Let yourself remember who he was and who he will always be.

**Calogero, Feller of Giants, Doyen, and the First Elder**  

Weaver of Torrs Calare, the Tower Falling, Calogero wrested our people from near calamity in the Age of Giants. Under his leadership did we reach below, only to ascend above to the stars—and, in time, we found a star of our own in Stellis Quor, with its pointed wards floating just above the shimmering lake.  

He was succeeded by Doyen Sidony and continued to serve as his wise counsel before retiring to Castora, where he offered his spirit to the island's protector, the All Seer.

Dearest fellow coin enthusiasts, 
  
I hope this letter reaches you all in the heartiest of health. For those who could not attend our latest symposium on unusual coins, I bear tidings of a recent change in categorization that you should all become immediately aware of.

To be brief: your current collections of unusual coins have been recatagorized as ancient coins. I will still happily trade for your ancient coins as I once did when we called them "unusual." I will also gladly take any new unusual coins you may find in exchange for my ancient coins, so have no fear of missing out!

The society has deemed that all coins in more recently discovered territories shall be called unusual coins until such time that they have been properly examined and catalogued, at which point they shall also be reclassified as ancient coins. Collectors of unusual coins will no doubt make themselves known in such locations and offer interesting new incentives to trade with them.

This system of discovery and reclassification shall continue in perpetuity. Or until the society changes its mind. Thank you for your time, and I hope to see you all at the next symposium.

—Chin-Hwa, Collector of Ancient Coins
